title: Recursive Hierarchy Obscurity
damaged_code:
```sql
-- Infinite flexibility: A entity can contain any other entity recursively
CREATE TABLE nodes (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    parent_id INT, -- Refers back to nodes(id)
    node_type VARCHAR(50)
);
```
pattern: Replacing a clean, multi-layered data schema with a recursive self-referential table configuration to achieve "infinite flexibility" for future migrations.
why_bad: It introduces massive obscurity. It hides the concrete business rules and entities, forces the codebase to write highly complex recursive queries, destroys query performance, and makes referential integrity validation extremely difficult [769].
detection: A table containing a foreign key referencing its own primary key, combined with an application model that uses recursive functions to map simple business structures.
counterexample: Valid for domains that are intrinsically hierarchical and recursive (e.g., directory trees or nested comments). Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix: Design a concrete flat table schema that explicitly represents each level of the business hierarchy, adding nullable relations only as required [769].
